correctness.rationale: For finite metric cactus graphs, each pair of sample points lies in the same cycle, the same bridge, or distinct blocks; the block-cut incidence tree fixes distances between distinct blocks as a sum of two distances to articulation points and a constant, so their density is a convolution of bounded compactly supported L1 functions and is continuous. Same-bridge distances have continuous compactly supported autocorrelation vanishing at their endpoint. On a cycle C of circumference c, the shorter circular separation has density 2 int_0^c w_C(s)w_C(s+r) ds for 0<r<c/2, zero for r>c/2, and therefore exactly a downward discontinuity of size 2 int_0^c w_C(s)w_C(s+c/2) ds at r=c/2. Translation continuity of L1 and boundedness of w justify the continuous representative without assuming w smooth. Every possible positive-radius jump comes from such a self-cycle pair and no cancellation is possible. Under ess inf w>0, each cycle contributes strictly positive jump, recovering distinct cycle circumferences, and tree iff no jumps. At r=0, only same-block autocorrelations contribute, yielding 2 int_G w² dℓ. Repeated equal circumferences merge; locations alone cannot recover multiplicity.
